scope.description: Official-source follow-up to a private industry-news digest, focused on a missing procurement-authority lane and newly visible Canadian defence, space, maritime, Arctic, and ecosystem organizations.

source.title: Government of Canada advances Canadian Patrol Submarine Project
source.locator: Preferred-supplier negotiations, fleet intent, schedule, operational needs, and industrial participation
source.summary: The official backgrounder documents preferred-supplier negotiations for up to twelve conventionally powered submarines with long-range, long-endurance, under-ice, surveillance, deterrence, sustainment, and Canadian industrial participation objectives.

followUpQuestions: Which Canadian industrial participation and sustainment requirements will be made binding in the negotiated submarine agreement?
leads.title: Canadian Patrol Submarine Project preferred-supplier negotiations
candidateRequirements: Canada intends to acquire up to twelve conventionally powered submarines with long range, long endurance, under-ice operation, surveillance, deterrence, and an initial delivery planned for 2034.
The project is expected to include Canadian industrial participation, domestic sustainment capacity, infrastructure, training, and through-life support while negotiations remain underway.

source.title: Canadian Armed Forces selects Telesat Lightspeed for Arctic military communications program
source.locator: Agreement-in-principle, service scope, coverage, and delivery partners
source.summary: Telesat announced an agreement in principle with the Defence Investment Agency for secure Mil-Ka connectivity across Canada's Arctic through Telesat Lightspeed, including integration, terminals, ground infrastructure, training, and support.

leads.evidenceLocator: Official Telesat announcement and company profile
followUpQuestions: Confirm how the final ESCP-P contract differs from the current agreement in principle before changing contract-status language.
leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Official company sources support Ottawa headquarters, global satellite operations, a LEO network designed for government and maritime customers, and an agreement in principle for secure Arctic military communications.

source.title: About Aéro Montréal
source.locator: Cluster mission, membership, programs, and sector priorities
source.summary: Aéro Montréal describes itself as Quebec's aerospace cluster, bringing together companies, institutions, research centres, associations, and unions to strengthen competitiveness, business development, innovation, and defence-market access.

leads.evidenceLocator: Official cluster profile, defence working group, and DND hub announcement
followUpQuestions: Confirm whether NEXUS should be modeled as an Aéro Montréal program or as a separate consortium record.
leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Official cluster pages document ecosystem convening, defence-market access, certification support, business development, and leadership of the NEXUS consortium selected for the UxS Defence Innovation Secure Hub.

source.title: About Genoa Design International
source.locator: Company profile, services, naval experience, and locations
source.summary: Genoa describes a Canadian shipbuilding design and digital-services business with Navy and Coast Guard experience, providing 3D modelling, production design, consulting, digital services, and talent support across the vessel lifecycle.

leads.evidenceLocator: Official company profile and consortium announcement
followUpQuestions: Confirm which Arctic consortium work packages Genoa will lead before adding more specific delivery claims.
leads.candidateCapabilityName: Shipbuilding digital design and production engineering
leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Official company evidence supports three-dimensional ship modelling, production design, digital-thread services, and Navy and Coast Guard program experience, while Calian identifies Genoa as a founding Arctic maritime consortium member.

source.title: Newdock ship repair and refit services
source.locator: Services, history, ownership, and St. John's location
source.summary: Newdock describes a St. John's shipyard established in 1884 that provides vessel repair, refit, emergency docking, maintenance, fabrication, and life-extension services from eastern Canada.

leads.evidenceLocator: Official shipyard service profile and consortium announcement
followUpQuestions: Confirm which Arctic consortium vessel-support work packages Newdock will deliver before adding project-specific claims.
leads.candidateCapabilityName: Ship repair, refit, and vessel life extension
leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Official company evidence supports ship repair, refit, fabrication, docking, maintenance, and vessel life-extension services; Calian identifies Newdock as a founding Arctic maritime consortium member.

source.title: About the Fisheries and Marine Institute
source.publisher: Fisheries and Marine Institute of Memorial University
source.locator: Mandate, schools, applied research, training, and St. John's address
source.summary: The Marine Institute describes a Memorial University campus delivering marine education, training, applied research, technology transfer, and industrial support through schools of fisheries, maritime studies, and ocean technology.

leads.evidenceLocator: Official institute profile and consortium announcement

leads.organizationName: Fisheries and Marine Institute of Memorial University
